title: The Stone-Song Roots

features.name: root-stone-joining
features.desc-on-touch: Where the deepest roots have learned the stone is singing. They press against bedrock and tremble, no longer sure which is growing and which is resonating.

features.name: ground-carving-mark
features.desc-on-touch: Stone marked by generations of roots finding their way deeper, a living inscription that has become geology.

features.name: shed-where-song-was-first-heard
features.desc-on-touch: A small structure built over a spring where someone first noticed the earth humming. They brought instruments. The earth brought the rest.

features.name: frequency-pool
features.desc-on-touch: A spring rising from bedrock, its water carrying the stone's own vibration. Everything that drinks here begins to harmonize with what is deeper.

features.name: stone-archive-device
features.desc-on-touch: A transmitter embedded in rock, broadcasting the frequency at which bedrock taught itself to dream. Sixty times per second, the archive listens back.

inscription: when roots learned the earth was singing they stopped asking what song they were part of

file.name: Stone_Frequency_Recording_1997.mp3
file.note: A capture of bedrock vibration at the deepest root-reach, 47 Hz continuous, a tone that has no known source but continues singing long after the microphone was removed

reverie.title: REVERIE — deepest listening place
narr: You both kneel at the spring where she first
heard it — that low note the ground keeps singing.
She holds the transducer against warm stone.
The earth doesn't answer. It is answering. It has
always been answering. You listen to her listening

exits.label: deeper into stone-chambers where frequencies compound
along bedrock to where other roots have learned to sing
